# Build table

Every build, one row each (moved out of DEV_NOTES.md in step 2, 2026-10-20, to keep the notes small; the rows are unchanged, in their old order, and the two blank lines that split the table are gone).
Each seat adds its own rows under its work's name; the build master adds the merge row with the real build number (CLAUDE.md "How we work").

From the old top of DEV_NOTES (history, not the current state):

### Current build: 0.60.7 (about 37,400 lines)

Two decks, joined by a working lift. Deck 4 (Quarters) plays as before. Deck 5 (Operations) is built and dressed: the Works complex, storage, machine shop, shuttle bay with the shuttle Tern, the door gear and the fan. Pell works there.

Deck 4's static screenshots are pixel-identical from 0.5.0 through 0.5.7. The only Deck 4 changes are the spine and lobbies (not in the harness views), and crew routes that shifted when Pell left and when the car and benches changed which tiles are walkable.

| 0.27.28 | Slow frames, cause 1 (section 8b, `CrowdChunk.rebuild`). A crowd group's mesh is rebuilt whenever someone joins, leaves, switches detail or picks up or puts down a prop. That's about 200 times a ship hour at dinner or breakfast, and it was the biggest cost inside slow frames (21–31%, plus most of the garbage collection). Each rebuild now keeps and reuses the group's arrays and GPU buffers, grown by half when too small and drawn with a draw range. The skin weights are written once, and only the slots from the first one that changed are rewritten and uploaded (`updateRange`). The pending range runs from the lowest change since the mesh was last drawn (`pv`/`pi`, reset in `onBeforeRender`, which r128 calls after the vertex upload and before the index upload). Without that, two rebuilds between draws lost the first one's upload, and cadet_test caught it. `crowd.stats()` reads the used counts (`c.nv`, `c.ni`). Same triangles in the same order. Rebuild time over a ship hour (desktop): dinner 242 → 95 ms (1.25 → 0.49 ms each), breakfast 321 → 88 ms (1.48 → 0.41 ms each). cadet_test vs 0.27.27 ALL IDENTICAL (every shot 0 px). 32 crowd shots at breakfast and dinner, with skipped frames between them, are identical. deck_check, day_check 1 and events_check OK. |
| 0.27.29 | Slow frames, cause 2 (section 7, `findPath`; the performance engineer owns section 7 for this change, by the lead's decision). The same search, made fast. The open tiles sit in a binary heap ordered by (f, the order each tile was first added), which is exactly the tile the old scan of the open list picked: the lowest f, the earliest in the list on a tie, with a duplicate entry counting from its node's first push. So every path is the same tile for tile, and the goal array itself is still the path's last element. Tiles are numbers (i * D + j) in typed arrays kept between calls (`_fp`, a stamp per call), and `free()`/`edgeOpen()` are asked at most once per tile or edge in a call. The avoid set's 'i,j' keys are read once. A start or goal off the grid goes to `findPathScan`, which is the old search, kept. Proof (`path_check.py`, new): 3,000 random searches per deck (open, blocked and off-grid tiles, a third with avoid sets, for nobody, the player or crew) all match, including every failure. So do all 1,131 real calls of a played Monday (06:00 to 23:00, Decks 3, 4, 5, 2), and 3,200 on a combine with sim 0.26.31. 3.3 to 4.1 times faster. Slow frames over a ship hour on that combine (0.60.2 + sim bfcd864 + galley 40166d6), 0.27.27 → 0.27.29 (with 0.27.28): frames over 4 ms dinner 36/31 → 17/19, breakfast 53/32 → 17/7; 99th percentile 4.1–4.8 → 2.4–3.2 ms; time inside slow frames dinner 141 → 56 ms, breakfast 196 → 74 ms. Also the 0.27.27 comment now says posing places the body too (reviewer 2b). cadet_test vs 0.27.28 ALL IDENTICAL; day_check 1 output identical to 0.27.28's line for line; deck_check, events_check, player_check (covering 0.27.28 too) OK. |

Measured with a stand-in on all 288 seat places on every deck (hips, knees, and the surface under each). Seat heights were right everywhere: the hips sit about 8 cm above the seat, as they should. The legs were the problem. They are too short to reach the floor with level thighs, so the feet-on-the-floor pose (`legIK` to 0.3 m ahead) sloped the thighs down, and the knees ended about 14 cm below the seat top. Now `seatCushion` (8b) casts one ray 0.3 m in front of the seat spot against the deck's furniture and keeps the answer on the person until they move. Where there's cushion near seat height, the thighs stay level just above it and the shins hang (feet may hang a little above the floor). Elsewhere it's unchanged, feet on the floor. After: 19 places still flag on my strict test, and they're not clipping. The bow lounge booths' 0.42 surface is the booth table (legs go under it, correct, and unchanged); the bridge window seats are the same. The rest are within a few cm on floor cushions. cadet_test vs 0.27.39: e_night 646 px behind the see-through location panel (a seated crew member's legs); all other shots within 1 level (renderer noise); all data identical. | 0.27.33 | The shadow stand-ins (0.27.25) are built over the frames after a deck change instead of inside `buildDeck`. `shadowStandIns()` now only lists what will cast through a stand-in, with each piece's matrix taken at build time as before. `shadowStep()` (section 12, once a frame, after `crowd.update`) does the triangle work, `SHADOW_STEP` (40,000) vertices a frame: counting first, then filling, then the stand-ins go in and the originals stop casting, all in the same frame. Until then the originals cast their own shadows, as before 0.27.25: the same depth from the same triangles, so the picture is the same at every moment. The work itself is faster: indexed geometry is read through its index (no `toNonIndexed` copy), the bucket name is reused while triangles stay in one 10×10 block, and the bounding sphere is worked out on the way (box while counting, radius while filling), exactly as `computeBoundingSphere` makes it. Desktop, warm: the old one-block cost D1 17–28, D2 88–122, D3 165–326, D4 57–70, D5 33–49, D6 13–19 ms inside the deck change; now D3 is 48 slices of ≤1.7 ms (56 ms in all), D4 24 slices ≤3.1 ms, the rest ≤2.6 ms a slice. On a phone (4× slower) that's about 6 ms a frame for 1–2 seconds instead of up to about 0.7 s of frozen deck change. Proof: every stand-in's triangles, face side, bounding sphere, follow and show-with link, and every mesh's castShadow, are bit-for-bit the same as 0.27.32's on all six decks (scratch probe sseq.py); only object id numbers differ (the stand-ins are made later). `unloadDeck` drops an unfinished job (`SHADOW_JOB`); leaving a deck 3 frames in, three rounds over Decks 3, 2 and 5, Deck 4's memory and object count come back the same. cadet_test vs 0.27.32: every shot pixel-identical; the one difference is the end-of-test GPU geometry count, 371 → 416, which is 0.27.24's number: while the stand-ins are being built, the old-style shadow pass uploads about 45 pieces that are off screen, and they stay uploaded until the deck is left. 54 more shots (six decks × three camera turns × 2, 12 and 120 frames after arriving, both while building and after): 0 pixels different. deck_check OK, path_check OK, day_check 1 OK. |

| 0.47.9 | Deck architect 5, the user's playtest report "a lot of speech bubbles are flickering" (on a phone: they shake or jump between two spots). **Causes:** (1) the bubbles were placed in `crowd.update`, before the camera followed you that frame, so each was drawn one frame's camera movement off its speaker, and on a phone's uneven frames that offset changed every frame (the shake); (2) two overlapping bubbles chose their sides by comparing their speakers' screen x every frame, so when the speakers stood close or crossed, both bubbles swapped sides in one frame (about 120 px each, the jump). **Fix:** `bubbles.tick(dt)` now only counts time down; the new `bubbles.place()` runs in the main loop just before the frame is drawn (`camera.updateMatrixWorld()` first), positions each bubble with a fractional-pixel `translate3d` (the `.bubw` CSS now `left:0;top:0;will-change:transform`), keeps a pair's left/right order and stacking until the speakers are clearly the other way round (24 px) or apart (12 px), and eases any change of layout over a few frames while following the speaker exactly. New **`bubble_check.py`**: phone size (390 × 844, devicePixelRatio 3), frames alternating 17 and 33 ms, you walking and the camera turning, two bubbles up: tail aim against the drawn speaker (0.5 px), no shake, no jump over 45 px, no hide/re-show within 30 frames, no side-swapping. On 0.47.8: FAILED (aim 3.4 px off, a 121 px jump); on 0.47.9: OK (0.00 px, largest move 3.4 px). Also: cadet_test differs only in b_wander10s and i_tap0, where a bubble is up: it sits a few px over, placed with the frame's own camera; lines_check PASS; deck_check OK. |

(3) **mech_check m17 'the paper part differs after the rides': a check problem.** It fails every run with the storm on and passes with it off. Cause: someone late for a meal tradition goes through the line for it (`tradMeal`); when its seats are all taken they eat standing ("the galley's counted them"), a real meal, but `evening()` only counted the tradition as eaten if a segment carried the tradition's tag, so it planned an ordinary dinner too (a second queue and a second tray, sometimes in the lounge). The breakfast tradition's check (`morning`) had the same gap.
